recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-31808 unless the work group later reopens the broader modeling question of whether Ingredient should remain a resource.
issue_request: FHIR-31808 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for R5. It objected to Ingredient being treated as an independently shareable thing and accepted reversing the direction of the relevant links: add references from Ingredient to the resources that use it and remove the product-resource pointers to Ingredient.
initial_application: The source history contains explicit FHIR#31808 commits fbfbf287b1 and 4b8f3f0577. They added Ingredient.for and changed MedicinalProductDefinition.ingredient, AdministrableProductDefinition.ingredient, and ManufacturedItemDefinition.ingredient from Ingredient references into CodeableConcept elements with guidance about incoming Ingredient references.
additional_context: Ingredient is active in the current build through source/fhir.ini. The current source still has Ingredient as a resource, which is consistent with the modified resolution rather than the issue title alone. Later Published issue FHIR-39515 explains that ManufacturedItemDefinition.component.constituent.hasIngredient is a secondary reference to an existing Ingredient mentioned elsewhere, not the main ingredient-reference direction FHIR-31808 reversed.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the authoritative source already contains Ingredient.for targeting MedicinalProductDefinition, AdministrableProductDefinition, and ManufacturedItemDefinition, and the three affected product-definition ingredient elements no longer target StructureDefinition/Ingredient.

related_jiras.note: Later Published clarification renamed locationForIngredient to hasIngredient and confirms that this remaining ManufacturedItemDefinition reference is a locator for an existing Ingredient, not a reversal of the FHIR-31808 model.
